e.text: A1 hits 16.3% vs benchmark 4.1%; asking the Critic how to push it further.

e.note: Reading results for A1, A2, A3

critique.summary: Early, full-length citywide targeted ads plus a high-affinity brand drop (Polaroid or Vice) are working: A1 and A2 reach 15.6–16.3% at about $600–640 per point, roughly four times better than the benchmark's 4.1% at $2399 per point, with word of mouth carrying about half of adoption. Late, expensive pop-ups are not working: A3's day 26 and day 31 pop-ups cost $5000 for 7% of credited adoption, leaving too little time for spread and halving reach to 8.0%.

findings.finding: A1 has the best mean and floor, 16.3% (p10 14.4%) at $600 per point, with Indie rock and Drag Race districts at 20.3%; social ads (20.0%, $6300) and the Polaroid drop (16.7%, $2000) carry it, while the five $300 cafés earn only 1.0–1.4% each.
A2 reaches 15.6% (p10 13.9%) at $637 per point; the Vice drop earns 16.6% for $2000, but the Happy Sad Confused read earns only 7.8% for $3050, and the Indie rock and Drag Race core gets just 17.0%.
A3 reaches 8.0% (p10 6.8%) at $1220 per point because the pop-ups land on days 26 and 31 and social ads stop at day 22, so each $2500 pop-up earns only 3.5%.
The benchmark reaches 4.1% at $2399 per point, and its three $450 street teams earn 0.0–0.6%, which confirms that untargeted spending in busy areas is wasted.

changes.change: Build on A1, but drop the three weakest cafés (Bushwick Bakery, Grass Roots Juicery and L'imprimerie, $900) and add the Vice drop (collab:A5707876) from day 0, running it alongside the Polaroid drop.
changes.why: Each brand drop earns about 16.7% of adoption for $2000, compared with roughly 1% for each $300 café.

changes.change: If the budget cannot cover both drops, trim social:city to about 28 days rather than cutting a drop, and keep the ads starting on day 0.
changes.why: Starting early gives word of mouth, which drives about 50% of adoption, the most time to spread, while the drops are the most efficient spend.

changes.change: Do not schedule any pop-ups after day 20; if one is used, place it at Nostrand Coffee in Clinton Hill (zone 2) by about day 10.
changes.why: A3's day 26 and day 31 pop-ups returned 3.5% each for $2500, and seeding earlier lets them spread before launch.

changes.change: Drop the Happy Sad Confused read and the street teams.
changes.why: The podcast read cost $3050 for 7.8% of adoption, and the street teams returned 0.0–2.1% each.

Late, expensive pop-ups are not working: A3's day 26 and day 31 pop-ups cost $5000 for 7% of credited adoption, leaving too little time for spread and halving reach to 8.0%.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for A1

plan.headline: Brooklyn cafés plus Polaroid drop reach about four times the benchmark's natural audience
plan.summary: The bet is five high-affinity cafés near Nitehawk, a Polaroid co-branded drop and fit-weighted citywide social ads, all running the full campaign so word of mouth has time to spread through Bushwick, East Williamsburg and Clinton Hill. Qloo taste data puts these cafés at 0.89–0.90 affinity, driven by A24, Euphoria and Greta Gerwig fans, and Polaroid at 0.95, so spend lands where the Lady Bird and Euphoria crowd already is. The simulation built on Qloo taste data projects reach of 16.4% of the natural audience (range 14.9%–18.0%), about 4x the benchmark's 4.1%, at $598 per point of reach versus $2,399; this is a projection, not a guarantee.

weeks.label: 5 weeks before launch
items: 35–34 days before launch: confirm all five café partners and install flyers and postcards by the register.
34 days before launch: start the targeted social ads across New York, weighted to best-fit areas.
34 days before launch: launch the co-branded Polaroid drop and announce it on social.

weeks.label: 4–2 weeks before launch
items: 28 days before launch: check café materials are visible and restocked; set up the Grass Roots Juicery juice-and-ticket combo.
21 days before launch: shift ad weight toward the creative and areas with the best ticket clicks.
14 days before launch: push weekend showtimes and the Polaroid giveaway at screenings in ads and café postcards.

weeks.label: 1 week before launch
items: 7 days before launch: restock all café postcards; remind partners of screening dates.
3 days before launch: final ad push in Bushwick, East Williamsburg and Clinton Hill.

weeks.label: Launch week
items: 0 days before launch: preview screenings open at Nitehawk Williamsburg with the Polaroid drop on site.
Throughout launch week: keep social ads and café materials running; encourage attendees to bring friends.

risks: Projections come from a simulation built on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee; real reach may fall outside 14.9%–18.0%.
Each café is credited with only about 1% of adoption; their value depends on word of mouth, which drives 49.3% of adoption in the model.
Reach is weak outside Brooklyn-leaning taste districts (10.5% in Podcasts, sitcoms and gaming); far-off audiences like Newark may not travel.
Social ads carry the largest share of results; poor creative or targeting would hurt the whole plan.
measure: Ticket sales by week, compared against the pace needed for the projected reach.
Social ad clicks and cost per ticket by neighborhood.
Postcard pickups and juice-combo redemptions at each café.
Polaroid drop engagement and referral or bring-a-friend mentions.
